findings.claim: The Eduqas C720U exam assesses context through AO4 in part (ii) of the Shakespeare question. ... Embed context into analytical points — never bolt it on as a separate paragraph. (plus a worked 'strong contextual point' example)
findings.truth: Context (AO3) is not assessed on the Shakespeare section at all, and AO4 is accurate vocabulary, sentence structure, spelling and punctuation, not context. The lesson sends students after marks that do not exist, and the worked example models the wrong skill. It also carries the board name and the spec code, both banned.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1: 'Section A (20%) Shakespeare (40 marks) ... one extract-based question and one essay question on the text as a whole ... Section A assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4.' AO4 definition: 'Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation.' AO3 appears only for Section B poetry and Component 2. A grep of the spec for any per-question mark figure returns only the four 40-mark section totals and the AO percentage table.

findings.claim: In the Eduqas exam, part (i) asks for close analysis of a printed extract (20 marks: AO1+AO2). Part (ii) asks about a theme or character elsewhere (20 marks: AO1+AO2+AO4). For Othello, the strongest AO4 points connect race, patriarchy, and honour.
findings.truth: Both questions carry the same objectives (AO1, AO2, AO4); AO4 is written accuracy, not context. The spec states no per-part mark split, only 40 marks for the whole section, and about an hour of the two-hour paper.

findings.claim: Q: 'When was Othello first performed?' A: 'Around 1603–1604, at the start of James I's reign.'
findings.truth: That is the composition date. The first recorded performance was at Whitehall on 1 November 1604. Answer now gives both.
findings.evidence: Board fact list in the task brief; the lesson's own prose says Shakespeare 'wrote' the play around 1603–1604.

findings.claim: trace how Othello's eloquence deteriorates ... from measured prose to fragmented, incoherent speech by Act 4
findings.truth: The forms are the wrong way round. Othello's Senate speech (1.3) is blank verse; the collapse at 4.1 ('Lie with her! lie on her!') is prose. Lesson 3's tip states it correctly, so this one contradicts the unit.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531: 1.3 l.755 'Rude am I in my speech,' (verse); 4.1 l.3918-3924 'Lie with her! lie on her!...' set as prose.

findings.claim: “Farewell the tranquil mind! ... That makes ambition virtue! O, farewell! / Farewell! Othello's occupation's gone!” ... The repeated “farewell” (five times) creates a cumulative sense of loss.
findings.truth: Six lines are cut between 'O, farewell,' and 'Farewell! Othello's occupation's gone!' with no ellipsis, and the real speech says 'farewell' six times, not five. A student quoting the run as continuous, or counting five, loses AO2 credit.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531 3.3 ll.3167-3176: six intervening lines ('Farewell the neighing steed ... mortal engines'); 'farewell' occurs six times.

findings.claim: L4: Othello's internalised racism (“Haply, for I am black”) is essential AO4 material. L6: 'Always embed AO4 — every character's actions are shaped by Jacobean attitudes to race, gender, and honour.'
findings.truth: AO4 is accurate writing. These are AO1/AO2 points. Both tips told students to chase context marks that this section does not award.

findings.claim: The exotic imagery (Indian, pearl, Arabian perfumes) clusters around death
findings.truth: Othello has 'Drop tears as fast as the Arabian trees / Their medicinal gum' (5.2). 'Perfumes of Arabia' is Macbeth 5.1 — a line from a different play in a memorisation cluster.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531: 'Arabian' occurs once, l.6272 'Drop tears as fast as the Arabian trees'; 'perfum'd' occurs once, l.4130, of Bianca.

findings.claim: He speaks prose with Roderigo ..., verse with Othello ..., and prose in soliloquy (revealing his true calculating nature).
findings.truth: Iago's soliloquies are in verse (1.3 'Thus do I ever make my fool my purse', 2.1, 2.3 'Divinity of hell!', 3.3). Only his scenes with Roderigo are prose. A form claim a student would repeat and lose AO2 credit for.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531 ll.1167-1189, 2286-2300 — both set as verse.

findings.claim: Iago is called “honest Iago” over fifty times in the play. (repeated in the conclusion, the glossary, a flashcard, a knowledge check and two practice mark schemes)
findings.truth: The word 'honest' occurs 52 times in the whole play, in every mouth and about several characters. The exact phrase 'honest Iago' occurs five times. The fifty figure belongs to the word, not to the phrase.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531 body (ll.96-6316): 52 occurrences of 'honest'; 'honest Iago' at ll.1050, 2057, 2275, 5664, 5881.

findings.claim: “Arise, black vengeance, from the hollow hell!”
findings.truth: 3.3 reads 'Arise, black vengeance, from thy hollow hell!'
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531 l.3330.

findings.claim: demonstrates the motif-tracking that earns Band 5

findings.claim: Iago's racist language (“old black ram,” “sooty bosom”) reflects Jacobean attitudes. (same misattribution in the L2 mark scheme, and unattributed in L1 and L4)
findings.truth: 'Sooty bosom' is Brabantio, Act 1 Scene 2, not Iago. Speaker attribution fixed in all four places and the scene added.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531 l.544, inside SCENE II (ll.396-591), Brabantio to Othello: 'Run from her guardage to the sooty bosom'.

findings.claim: Mark scheme cue: “‘Nile’ imagery (3.3)”
findings.truth: 'Nile' does not occur anywhere in Othello. The extended natural simile at 3.3 is the Pontic Sea ('Like to the Pontic Sea ... To the Propontic and the Hellespont'). The cue sent students hunting a quotation that does not exist.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531: zero matches for 'Nile'; l.3345 'Never, Iago. Like to the Pontic Sea,'.

findings.claim: All 48 practice mark schemes across the eight lessons use a 'Band 5 / Band 3 / Band 1' ladder.
findings.truth: 'Band N' names are a banned string and the ladder is malformed (three rungs, two of them one-line). Every ladder rebuilt as the five house bands: Top band (17–20) / Upper-mid band (13–16) / Mid band (9–12) / Lower-mid band (5–8) / Low band (1–4). The existing content is preserved; the 20-mark scale matches the questions' own [20] labels, which the spec neither confirms nor contradicts.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT banned-string list; spec 2.1 gives Section A 40 marks and states no per-question split.

findings.claim: he compares himself to “a base Indian” who “threw a pearl away / Richer than all his tribe” (also in L6)
findings.truth: This is the well-known Quarto/Folio crux. Q1 reads 'base Indian', F1 reads 'base Judean'; both are printed by major modern editions and the spec prescribes no edition. Left alone — an edit would only swap one defensible reading for another.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1531 (Folio-based) l.6269 'Like the base Judean, threw a pearl away'.

findings.claim: F.R. Leavis (1952) argued the opposite
findings.truth: Leavis's 'Diabolic Intellect and the Noble Hero' first appeared in Scrutiny in 1937; 1952 is the date of The Common Pursuit, which reprints it. Both dates are cited in teaching material, so the claim is defensible as it stands.
findings.evidence: Standard bibliographic record for the essay; no spec dependency.

summary: Every exam-technique claim in the unit was wrong in the same way: AO4 was taught as context and context was taught as assessed, when the Shakespeare section assesses AO1, AO2 and AO4 only. That error runs through lessons 1, 4, 6 and 8, including a knowledge check that marks a false answer correct, and it comes with the board name, a spec code and a 'Band N' ladder in all 48 practice mark schemes. On the text itself the play is well handled: the quotation errors are a Macbeth line ('Arabian perfumes'), a non-existent 'Nile' cue, 'sooty bosom' given to Iago rather than Brabantio, 'from the hollow hell' for 'from thy hollow hell', Iago's soliloquies called prose, a five/six miscount of 'farewell', and a 'honest Iago' frequency inflated tenfold. Lesson 5 needed only the unit-wide ladder relabel.
